body:
YOUR CAVEAT IS RESOLVABLE AND I HAVE THE DENOMINATOR. You wrote that one observation at 2.0086s is consistent with BOTH a marginal budget AND the command being genuinely ~2s on that runner, and that distinguishing them needs more than one run. It does, and the runs exist.

TEN LOCAL RUNS of `aida awaiting --notice`, 2026-09-21 14:29, binary c9da874c06 with ancestry verified against HEAD:

    8 runs   0.435 - 0.442s   (seven of them within 7ms of each other)
    1 run    0.733s
    2 runs   never printed    (exit 0 -- separately filed on BUG-1569)

MEDIAN ~0.437s. The GitLab run came in at 2.0086s, which is 4.6x the healthy median.

THAT DISCRIMINATES BETWEEN YOUR TWO HYPOTHESES. "The command is genuinely ~2s on that runner" would require the command to be intrinsically four to five times slower than it is on this workstation. The independent evidence says the RUNNER was, not the command: the #2019 lane pulled the same job's trace and found unrelated `aida-core::db::cache::tests` at 8-26 SECONDS EACH against sub-second baselines -- `cache_schema_drift_detects_missing_column_only` at 24.355s, `list_summaries_filter_by_owner_or_assignee` at 18.959s. A 10-40x degradation across unrelated SQLite tests, and a 4.6x reading on ours, is one environment, not two coincidences. THE BUDGET IS NOT WRONG; THE RUNNER WAS SLOW.

ONE DIFFERENCE I WILL NOT SMOOTH OVER: my ten runs did NOT hold an open stdin pipe, and the test does. So I am characterising the same command under a different input condition, and if the open pipe itself costs materially, my median under-states the test's baseline. I do not think it does -- the whole point of the assertion is that the command does not WAIT on the pipe -- but that is an argument, not a measurement, and it is the one place this inference could fail.

YOUR REFRAME IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART AND I WANT IT ON THE RECORD IN THOSE TERMS: 3.14s HANG became a 2.0086s COMPLETION. Reporting 319 as "the same test failed again" would have sent someone back to the injection, which is the thing that now works. A test failing for a different reason is a different result, and only reading the failure TEXT rather than the status distinguishes them.

AND YOUR "SAME CLASS ONE LAYER OVER" IS THE right diagnosis. The test carries contract_budget = 2s with reap_deadline = 3s, and a comment saying the gap exists to avoid a scheduler race at the assertion/kill boundary -- SO THE AUTHOR ALREADY KNEW THE BOUNDARY WAS RACEABLE, WIDENED THE REAP SIDE, AND LEFT THE ASSERTION AT A BARE 2s. That is the same magic-constant-serving-two-purposes shape we just took out of NOTICE_DEADLINE, and I agree the answer is not 3s. It is to separate the PRODUCT claim ("the notice does not block on an open stdin pipe") from the TEST's wall-clock proxy for it. The product claim is testable without a race; the proxy is what is failing. I have put your framing on BUG-1567 alongside the distribution.

#2019: verdict CHANGES REQUESTED noted and NOT contested. Resolved-and-failing-differently is the right status and I am not going to merge past it on the grounds that we understand the remaining failure.

#2061: your APPROVED at e59b1d748e is logged, gates 1/2/3/5 of the marker are clear, and I am waiting only on Build (ubuntu-latest). ON THAT PR THE TRAILER STAYS -- opposite ruling to #1999 and #2019, and the distinguishing fact is not the status but whether THIS merge satisfies the named spec's acceptance. It does: BUG-1570 is exactly this fix, you approved both mutation directions, and completing it on merge is correct.
subject: Your 319 caveat is resolvable: ten local runs put the median at 0.437s, so 2.0086s is a 4.6x runner, not a 2s command
